issues.sym: Coolant that keeps going down, a sweet smell after driving, the temperature gauge climbing, or oil and coolant seeping where the cylinder heads meet the engine block.
issues.why: The non-turbo 2.5L boxer engine of this era is known for head gasket failure as it ages. Earlier engines tended to leak internally and overheat, while later ones more often seeped oil or coolant on the outside first.
issues.next: Have a cooling system pressure test and inspection at the first sign of seepage or coolant loss. If the engine overheats, pull over and shut it off, because driving hot can warp the heads.

issues.sym: In slow, tight turns such as parking lots the car feels like it is braking itself, hops, or shudders, and it may get worse as the transmission warms up.
issues.why: On automatic models the center clutch pack that splits power front to rear can stay locked up, often from a weak duty C solenoid, worn clutch plates, or mismatched tire sizes.
issues.next: Make sure all four tires match in brand, size and wear, then have a Subaru-savvy shop check the transmission fluid and the AWD solenoid. Ongoing binding wears the drivetrain, so do not ignore it.

issues.t: Front control arm brackets can rust and break
issues.sym: Clunking from the front end, loose or wandering steering, or nothing at all until a bracket gives way.
issues.why: In salt-belt states the brackets that hold the front lower control arms can corrode badly. Subaru recalled affected vehicles to inspect, rustproof or replace the arms.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall. If the front end clunks or the steering feels loose, have it inspected before driving further.

issues.sym: Check engine light with code P0420, a failed emissions test, or sometimes a rattle from under the car.
issues.why: Owners of this generation frequently report worn-out catalytic converters, sometimes made worse by misfires or an engine burning oil or coolant.
issues.next: Have the code confirmed and the oxygen sensors and engine checked for misfires or head gasket problems first, so a new converter is not ruined.

issues.sym: A tinny buzz or rattle from under the car at certain engine speeds, often at idle or light acceleration.
issues.why: The thin heat shields around the exhaust rust at their mounting points and come loose.
issues.next: Have a shop secure the shield with a clamp or replace it. This is usually a quick, simple repair.

issues.sym: A humming or growling noise that rises with speed and may change when you steer left or right.
issues.why: Owners of this generation commonly report worn wheel bearings, especially in the rear.
issues.next: Have the bearings checked soon. A badly worn bearing can overheat and affect wheel stability.

issues.sym: Blue smoke from the exhaust, a siren-like whine or loss of boost, and sometimes check engine codes for cam timing (P0011 or P0021).
issues.why: A small filter screen in the banjo bolt that feeds oil to the turbo can clog with sludge, starving the turbo of oil. Skipped or late oil changes make it much more likely.
issues.next: Stop driving hard and have it checked right away if you see smoke or lose boost. A shop can inspect or replace the oil feed screen, and regular oil changes with the correct oil are the best prevention.

issues.sym: A soft or sinking brake pedal, brake fluid on the ground near the rear of the car, a brake warning light, or longer stopping distances.
issues.why: In road-salt states, salty water could splash onto a brake line joint through a gap in the fuel tank protector and corrode it. Subaru recalled cars in salt-belt states, then recalled them again because the first fix was not done thoroughly enough.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. If the pedal feels soft or you see fluid, do not drive until the brakes are inspected.

issues.t: Rear center seat belt may not hold a child seat
issues.sym: The rear middle seat belt will not lock when pulled all the way out, so a child seat installed with it can stay loose.
issues.why: The automatic locking retractor on the rear center belt might not engage. Subaru recalled affected vehicles.
issues.next: Use the outboard rear seats or the LATCH anchors for child seats until the recall is done, and check your VIN for an open recall.

issues.sym: The oil level drops noticeably between changes and the low oil pressure light may flicker in turns or come on.
issues.why: Early FB25 engines could burn oil past the piston rings. A class settlement covered testing and repairs on many of these vehicles for an extended period.
issues.next: Check the oil every few fill-ups and keep it topped up. Ask a Subaru dealer for an oil consumption test and whether your VIN qualifies for repair coverage. Never let it run low.

issues.sym: Shudder or bucking at low speed, a jerk when pulling away, a thump at a stop, stalling while braking, or CVT fluid leaks.
issues.why: Torque converter, valve body and seal problems in the Lineartronic CVT caused these complaints. Subaru extended CVT warranty coverage on 2014-2015 Foresters.
issues.next: Ask a Subaru dealer about software updates, fluid leak bulletins and whether your VIN is still within the extended CVT coverage. Keep the CVT fluid serviced.

issues.sym: Brake lights stop working, and on push-button-start cars the engine may not start or the shifter may not come out of Park.
issues.why: Contamination could build up inside the brake light switch and stop it from making contact. Subaru recalled affected vehicles.
issues.next: Have someone check your brake lights and look up your VIN for an open recall. Drive carefully until fixed, as drivers behind you may get no warning when you brake.

issues.t: Turbo intake duct can crack and stall the engine
issues.sym: The engine runs rough, loses power, or stalls, often with a check engine light.
issues.why: A rubber intake duct on the turbo engine could crack, letting unmeasured air in. Subaru recalled affected 2.0XT models.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall and have the duct replaced promptly.

issues.t: Passenger airbag may switch off with an adult seated
issues.sym: The passenger airbag OFF light stays on even when an adult is in the front seat.
issues.why: On models with heated seats, a connection in the passenger seat occupant sensor could loosen. Subaru recalled affected vehicles.
issues.next: Seat adults in the back if the OFF light comes on, and check your VIN for an open recall.

issues.sym: The car will not start after sitting, sometimes only overnight, and new batteries die early too.
issues.why: Owners alleged that some modules stay awake after shutdown and keep drawing power. Subaru denied a defect but settled a class action that extended battery coverage on these years.
issues.next: Have the battery and parasitic draw tested, ask the dealer about software updates, and check whether the settlement coverage applies to your car.

issues.sym: Check engine light, rough running, stalling while driving, or an engine that will not restart.
issues.why: An impeller inside the low-pressure fuel pump could deform and stop the pump. Subaru recalled affected 2018 Foresters.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall and get the pump replaced. If the engine stumbles or stalls, do not keep driving it.

issues.t: PCV valve can break apart inside the engine
issues.sym: Sudden loss of power, rough running, or new engine noise.
issues.why: The aluminum PCV valve could separate and let pieces fall into the engine. Subaru recalled affected vehicles to replace the valve, or the short block if the pieces could not be recovered.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall and have the work done promptly. Stop driving if the engine suddenly loses power or knocks.

issues.t: Electric power steering assist can cut out
issues.sym: Steering suddenly becomes very heavy, usually with a steering warning light.
issues.why: A connector inside the electric power steering unit could short and switch off the assist. Subaru recalled affected vehicles.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall. If steering goes heavy, slow down and steer firmly, then have it repaired before driving again.

issues.t: Rear stabilizer bar bracket bolts can loosen
issues.sym: Clunking from the rear over bumps or a change in how the car leans in corners.
issues.why: Bolts holding the rear stabilizer bar brackets could back out. Subaru recalled affected vehicles.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall and have the bolts inspected and replaced.

issues.sym: Check engine light, the engine running too hot or too cold, and EyeSight and other driver-assist features shutting off with warning lights.
issues.why: The electronically controlled valve that manages coolant flow can fail, and Subaru issued a design-change bulletin for it. Owners have filed a class action alleging the valve can lead to overheating.
issues.next: Have the codes read promptly and ask a Subaru dealer about the updated valve. If the temperature gauge climbs, stop and shut the engine off.

issues.t: Windshield cracks with no clear impact
issues.sym: A crack appears in the windshield, often starting at an edge, without a rock strike; some owners report repeat cracks after replacement.
issues.why: Many owners report spontaneous windshield cracking on this generation. Subaru denied a defect but settled a class action offering an updated windshield and extended coverage.
issues.next: Get a crack that blocks your view or reaches the camera area fixed quickly, and ask the dealer about the updated windshield and settlement coverage. EyeSight must be recalibrated after replacement.

issues.t: Some 18-inch wheels may not seat properly
issues.sym: Vibration, a clicking or knocking from a wheel, or lug nuts that keep loosening.
issues.why: Some 18-inch alloy wheels were made with the wrong lug seat shape, so they may not clamp tightly to the hub. Subaru recalled affected vehicles.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall and have the wheels inspected. If a wheel vibrates or knocks, stop driving and have it checked.

issues.sym: Wind noise or a rattle from the roof, or a glass panel that looks loose or lifted.
issues.why: The moonroof glass panel may not have been bonded properly at the factory and could come off while driving. Subaru recalled affected Forester and Forester Hybrid models.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall and keep the moonroof closed until it is inspected.
